title: A large Fourier coefficient for a nonconstant Boolean function
statement: Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be nonconstant. Write $V$ for its variance under the uniform measure, $I$ for its total influence, $D=\lceil 8I/V\rceil$, and $\tau=(V/8)^2 I^{-2}9^{-D}$. Let $J$ be the set of coordinates whose Boolean influence is at least $\tau$. Then some nonempty set $S\subseteq[n]$ with $|S|\le D$ satisfies $\widehat f(S)^2\ge V/[2(D+1)(|J|+1)^D]$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
caveat: The formal statement relies on an undeclared predicate for nonconstancy; the statement renders it as the ordinary condition that $f$ is nonconstant.
